title: Lock in the win, hope on the loss
situation: You have two demo trades open. One is 30 pips in profit. The other is 35 pips down and close to its [[stop-loss|stop loss]]. You want to close the winner now to lock something in, and remove the stop on the loser so it has time to come back.
question: What do you do?

responses.text: Close the winner and remove the stop on the loser.
responses.explanation: This is the pattern that leads to small wins and large losses. Without a stop, the losing trade has no limit.

responses.text: Close both trades now to end the discomfort.
responses.explanation: This does stop the risk. But it is a decision made to escape a feeling, not one from your plan, so it tells you little about the plan.

responses.text: Leave the winner, but move the stop on the loser a bit further away.
responses.explanation: Moving a stop further away makes the loss you agreed to bigger.

responses.text: Leave both trades with the stops and [[take-profit|targets]] you planned.
responses.explanation: Loss aversion means losses feel bigger than gains of the same size. Your planned levels were set before that feeling kicked in.

takeaway: Losses feel bigger than equal gains. Planned stops and targets stop you acting on that feeling.
